sentences: All three are present on an RTX 4060 Ti (and an RTX 2060 SUPER), and `runtime/test/vk_harness.cpp` enables them when available, as does the runtime's `create_vulkan_device_standalone`, each with its extension (`VulkanDeviceInfo::fragment_shader_barycentric`, `fragment_shader_interlock`, `maintenance8`; checked by `d3d12_vulkan_device_test`).

All three are present on an RTX 4060 Ti, and `runtime/test/vk_harness.cpp` enables them when available. (It is guarded by the header macro `VK_KHR_MAINTENANCE_8_EXTENSION_NAME`, so older Vulkan headers build without it.
`vk_texture_test` enables it too, and `shaderImageGatherExtended`.) A device without `fragmentShaderBarycentric` (NVIDIA Pascal) runs the raw-barycentric PS with `--bary-fallback` (below).

Shaders translated with `--fma khr` need `VK_KHR_shader_fma` and its `shaderFmaFloat32` feature (`VkPhysicalDeviceShaderFmaFeaturesKHR`): `create_vulkan_device_standalone`, `runtime/test/vk_test_device.h` and the `vk_*` test programs enable it when the device offers it (`VulkanDeviceInfo::shader_fma`), and a test program refuses (exit 77) a module with `OpCapability FMAKHR` on a device without it.
